windows_ci_failure.what: PR #82's CI at its previous head 53d1bdf: the Windows leg failed four cases and every other job passed. The commit measured here fixes their causes (below); the CI cells above stay pending until the run at the new head
windows_ci_failure.head: 53d1bdf6354e4b19ebaa52de75d6d291f792e89e

causes.seen: link_target_missing's text was '\\?\C:\...\unmounted\data', the test expects the text the link was made with, 'C:\...\unmounted\data'
causes.cause: the walk took a link's text from os.readlink, which on Windows gives the reparse point's substitute name: an extended-length prefix for an absolute target and always for a junction
causes.fix: the walk keeps the text without the prefix (_platform.plain_path); a relative text, the only one made again, has none, so the links made again and the ledger's comparisons of them are as they were

causes.cause: os.open goes through the C runtime's _wopen, which reports a sharing violation (WinError 32) by errno EACCES alone, the OSError carrying no winerror, so _unreadable_error could not tell it from a permission denied
causes.fix: a source file is opened by _platform.open_for_reading: on Windows CreateFile with the access and sharing _wopen asks for (GENERIC_READ, FILE_SHARE_READ | FILE_SHARE_WRITE), the descriptor the C runtime's for that handle, so the refusal keeps WinError 32; POSIX opens as before (O_RDONLY | O_NONBLOCK). A lock violation (33) met while reading still comes through the C runtime by errno alone (CONTRACTS G, not run)

causes.seen: the destination did not read an older kit's 'C:\...\src/tables/t.parquet' as tables/t.parquet (read_as missing) and a 0.5.0 run's tables/t.parquet lost its inferred producer; the source read both
causes.cause: MigrationMapping compared an absolute path with the root's spellings as text split on os.sep only, so a path with both separators was not under 'C:\...\src'; the source's reader (legacy_identity) reads it through os.path.normpath
causes.fix: the mapping reads absolute paths and spellings as legacy_identity does (normpath after the extended-length prefix is dropped): on Windows either separator, and `..` folded as text, as the source's reader folds it
